title: which quantity does the producer's own comparison put the gate against, and is that the quantity the leg compares?

join_rules.publish_site: a line in a script naming the face that binds the gate's last path key either as a mapping value (`"tol": X`) or an item (`x["tol"] = X`)
join_rules.alias_chain: the published expression, if a bare identifier, plus parameter defaults `def f(p=X)` and plain rebinds `p = X` on the same file
join_rules.comparison: a line carrying an alias of the gate next to a comparison operator; operands = identifiers on both sides of the comparator, gate excluded, split on and/or
join_rules.operand_identity: the leg's own names (extracted face keys + expression identifiers) intersected with the operand names and the identifiers one hop down their definitions

notes: a name-level overlap is a LOWER bound on identity: two code paths may compute the same quantity under different names (invisible here) and two different quantities may share a short local name (r, b) -- every row publishes both name sets so the reading is re-checkable by eye and neither direction is claimed as proof
the band arithmetic of E308 is untouched; this study only re-scopes it, so a row can gain a producer comparison and still fail the operand test
a gate used to decide whether a measurement is possible (the bandexp ladder) is a feasibility test, not a tolerance on the number the leg compares
